text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Group of Fifteen in Dublin reach agreement on "monetary stability pact" to ensure fiscal discipline within economic and monetary union, which says that governments who join EMU but allow their budget deficits to exceed three percent of GDP will face sanctions, and fines. Franc and deutsche mark rise on news of agreement. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro).

-- A planned Boeing and McDonnell Douglas merger to create a 200-billion-franc turnover group, makes it urgent for European Airbus consortium to shift to limited company status to fend off giant competitor.
-- Groupe Andre posts a 918-million-franc loss for 1995-96 year.
-- State-owned TV channels France 2 and France 3 to undergo savings plan designed to save some 205 million francs at France 2, 20 million at France 3.
-- Company heads expect a dull end for 1996, due to economic and political uncertainty.
-- Association of Corporate Treasurers expects a 1.8 percent growth in 1997, up from an estimated 1.3 for 1996. --
-- Credit Lyonnais reshuffles private clients banking, develops alternative sales networks on telephone or computers, improves branch profitability with wider opening hours.
-- British retail group Marks and Spencer to tackle Eastern Europe and Asian markets, develop new products and services.
-- There will be a new tax on sales of meat from 1997, to finance improvements in the disposal of carcasses which are made necessary by scare of BSE "mad cow" disease.
